title: AI Images, Video and Voices: Module Quiz

cards.prompt: You pause an AI image tool halfway through "a lighthouse in a storm". What would you most likely see?

options.text: Rough shapes and colours, with no fine details yet
The top half finished, the bottom half still blank
The finished picture, just smaller and lower quality
Bits of real lighthouse photos, waiting to be joined

cards.explanation: The picture is cleared from static **all over at once**, rough to fine. It isn't drawn top to bottom or stuck together from saved photos.

cards.prompt: A picture of a famous footballer at a small local café is spreading. Hands, signs and shadows all look fine.

choices.text: Share it: it passed every check for AI mistakes
choices.consequence: Good AI pictures often have no give-aways, so that proves nothing. Find where it came from.

choices.text: Zoom in even closer and look for smaller mistakes
choices.consequence: Still nothing odd, and still no proof. Staring can't tell you if it's real.

choices.text: Search with the picture to find where it began
choices.consequence: It first appeared on an account that posts AI pictures, captioned as made with AI.

cards.explanation: **No give-aways proves nothing.** Check from outside the picture: **where it first appeared**, trusted news and who posted it.

cards.prompt: Is each one a **possible clue** that a picture is AI-made, or **not a clue**?

items.label: A mirror reflection that doesn't match
A shop sign with jumbled letters
A grainy photo from a concert
A blurry photo of a dog running

cards.explanation: A reflection that doesn't match and jumbled letters can be AI give-aways. Grainy and blurry photos are just normal photos.

cards.prompt: A viral picture has no watermark. Your friend says that proves it's real. Are they right?

options.text: Yes: AI tools always add a watermark you can see
Yes: a hidden watermark would show when it's shared
No: marks get cropped off, and many tools add none
No: a picture with no watermark is always made by AI

cards.explanation: Watermarks get cropped, screenshots can lose hidden file data, and many tools add none. No watermark proves **nothing** either way.

cards.prompt: A video of your principal says school's closed tomorrow. It's spreading in a chat started by someone you don't know.

steps.text: What's the best thing to do?

choices.text: Watch it again to check the lips match the words
choices.consequence: They match: good fakes pass that test. Check with the real source instead.

choices.text: Check the school's website, or have a parent call
choices.consequence: The school says it's open as normal. The video was a deepfake.

choices.text: Ask the group chat whether anyone knows if it's real
choices.consequence: People there have only seen the same video. Check with the real source, another way.

cards.explanation: An unknown sender and a surprising message are **situation clues**. Check with the real source another way: the school's website or a call.

cards.prompt: Is each use of face and voice AI **helpful** or **harmful**?

items.label: An author's voice cloned, with their OK
A video translated with the speaker's OK
A fake call to get bank details
A fake video of a classmate as a prank

cards.explanation: With the person's **permission** and nobody fooled, it helps. Fakes that trick or embarrass people harm.

cards.prompt: Match each situation to the right term.

pairs.left: An app turns your words into a painting
Video of a real singer saying fake words
An AI call sounding just like your aunt
Hidden data saying AI made a picture

cards.explanation: Making something new from words is **generative AI**; a fake video of a real person is a **deepfake**; an AI copy of a voice is a **voice clone**; a mark saying AI made it is a **watermark**.
